Question Choices: A student chooses 4 games from 9 available games. How many selections are possible? Input C(... ...) and P(... ...) for combination and permutation.
There are P(8,3)=336 ordered selections of three objects. How many unordered groups do they represent? Input C(... ...) and P(... ...) for combination and permutation.
Hints: Each group of 3 has 3! orders;Divide 336 by 6
Solution: Each unordered group is counted $3!=6$ times.;Thus $336/6=56=C(8,3)$.

Question Choices: A 5-person committee is chosen from 12 students and must include Alex. How many committees are possible? Input C(... ...) and P(... ...) for combination and permutation.
Hints: Include Alex first;Choose the other 4 members from the remaining 11 students
Solution: With Alex already included, choose 4 of the other 11 students.;The count is $C(11,4)=330$.

Question Choices: A bag contains 5 different red tokens and 6 different blue tokens. How many ways can 2 red and 2 blue tokens be selected? Input C(... ...) and P(... ...) for combination and permutation.
Hints: Choose the red tokens and blue tokens separately;Multiply $C(5,2)$ by $C(6,2)$
Solution: There are $C(5,2)=10$ red selections and $C(6,2)=15$ blue selections.;The total is $10\cdot15=150$.
